subject: Staged disclosure & subprocessor access — FinBridge incident playbook discussion
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Request: disclosure windows & subprocessor access for FinBridge incident playbook

Marissa / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. To make our playbook concrete, FinBridge needs written confirmation on a few items we expect to contractually bind into our DPA addendum:

1) Disclosure timing: we need an agreed maximum time-to-deliver specific artifact classes after Redwood confirms an incident that affects FinBridge customer data. Our regulator expects an "identified user list" within 48 hours for certain PII exposures. For other telemetry/forensic slices we can accept a longer window, but we need the categories and timelines codified.

2) Artifact scope / packaging: describe exactly what you will include in the forensic snapshot (telemetry ranges, logs, KV-cache dump, model traces, hashed identifiers vs plain text). Preferred: a machine-readable manifest and a packaged tarball with checksums.

3) Subprocessor access: will Redwood require subprocessors to participate in collection or transfer? If so, what approval process and background checks are performed? We require SOC2 recency, minimum background screen, and documented access justification.

4) Cross-border & transfer controls: confirm whether any artifacts will travel outside the US and proposed controls (encrypted S3 with customer-managed KMS, presigned URL expiry, etc.).

Can you please provide a draft operational timeline and any proposed redlines (we attached our checklist)? Ideally we'd like to turn this into an addendum within 10 business days.

Thanks —
Maya Singh
Head of Security Operations
FinBridge
Attachment: FinBridge-Security-Checklist.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 12:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: disclosure windows & subprocessor access for FinBridge incident playbook

Maya —

Appreciate the checklist and the clear asks. Below is a pragmatic draft we can operationalize quickly; I pulled in Kim from Legal to confirm DPA alignment. High level: we propose a "staged disclosure" approach that balances regulator speed with forensic completeness.

Proposed operational timeline (draft):
- Stage A (emergency indicators): within 8 hours of confirmed incident we will notify FinBridge with a summary and immediate containment measures.
- Stage B (critical identifiers): within 72 hours deliver an encrypted list of affected identifiers (hashed by default). If FinBridge needs a cleartext identified-user list for regulatory reasons, we can prioritize a redaction-validated cleartext export — target 48 hours but only with documented legal justification.
- Stage C (forensic package): within 10 business days deliver the full forensic package (logs, telemetry slices, model KV snapshots where applicable) packaged with manifest and checksums.

Artifact packaging: we will provide
- README manifest (JSON) listing file names, time ranges, and checksums
- logs.tar.gz (rotated, compressed), telemetry_slice.parquet, kv-cache-dump.ndjson (where applicable)
- chain_of_custody.txt with MD5/SHA256 and who accessed the package

Subprocessor access: Redwood will engage subprocessors only when necessary to collect ephemeral runtime artifacts (e.g., a managed GPU provider for memory dump). Standard practice:
- Subprocessor vetting: SOC2 Type II within 12 months or equivalent, basic background checks, and a documented access justification
- Access controls: time-limited credentials, customer-scoped buckets, and audit logs
- Exception: in exigent circumstances where immediate containment by a subprocessor is required to mitigate ongoing exfiltration, Redwood will notify FinBridge within the Stage A update and escalate for retroactive acknowledgement.

Cross-border: by default we will only export artifacts from the region where the data resides. If cross-border transfer is needed we will use customer-managed KMS + presigned links with short expiry (7 days) unless you request alternate controls.

I've attached our initial redlines for Section 7 (evidence & notification). If this looks reasonable I can route to our Contracts team and send an addendum for signature.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_redlines_section7.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: disclosure windows & subprocessor access for FinBridge incident playbook

Maya / Marissa —

Couple of legal clarifications to make the addendum actionable:

1) "Identified user list" language — we can commit to the 48-hour delivery for a narrowly scoping deliverable limited to (a) user identifiers that meet your regulator's definition and (b) logs required to demonstrate scope. That deliverable will be limited to identifiers + event timestamps and will exclude payloads unless you provide a lawful basis and a signed request form.

2) Forensic snapshot TTL — to preserve reproducibility we propose Redwood retain the forensic snapshot for 90 days, unless FinBridge requests longer archival. During retention we will maintain read-only storage and will not reprocess unless requested.

3) Subprocessor participation — any subprocessor asked to perform active collection will be bound by Redwood's subprocessor addendum and must attest SOC2 within 12 months, provide a minimal access justification, and accept the same confidentiality obligations. We will provide the vetting receipts on request.

4) Transfer controls — recommended: customer-managed KMS + presigned URLs w/ 7-day expiry OR downloadable package to a customer-owned bucket. We cannot hard-delete S3 objects in some 3rd-party-managed environments immediately; we will provide documented deletion steps and a deletion-confirmation proof.

If acceptable, I will draft tightened contract language to codify: 48h-limited-identifier-deliverable / 72h-expanded-deliverable / 10-business-day for full forensics; retention and subprocessor vetting clauses are included. Also attaching our DPA section cross-check.

-Kim
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dpa-sct.pdf
From: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@finbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: disclosure windows & subprocessor access for FinBridge incident playbook

Marissa / Kim —

This looks good and very thorough. Quick notes from FinBridge legal & ops:

- We appreciate the staged approach. Our regulator requires an identified-user list within 48 hours for certain PII classes; we can accept your 72-hour default but request an explicit path to 48h for the identified-list if we provide (a) a documented legal justification and (b) a signed addendum.
- Regarding subprocessors: we need to see the vetting receipts up-front for any new subprocessor who will have access to raw artifacts (even time-limited). If you can provide a list of the potential subprocessors and their SOC2 attestations, we can pre-approve to avoid blocking a live containment action.
- DocuSign: please send the addendum link and we'll get countersign by EOD.

FinBridge SOC ticket: https://finbridge.atlassian.net/browse/SOC-4128

Eliot Turner
Senior Manager, Incident Response
FinBridge
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@finbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 16:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: disclosure windows & subprocessor access for FinBridge incident playbook

Eliot —

Thanks — we can do that. Confirming the final operational points we've agreed to internally and will put into the addendum:

- 48-hour pathway: Redwood will deliver a limited "identified-user" export within 48 hours only when FinBridge provides (1) a regulator-cited legal justification and (2) an executed addendum. The 48-hour export is scoped to identifiers + event timestamps and will exclude payloads unless otherwise authorized.

- Default timeline: 72 hours for expanded identifier lists (hashed-by-default) and 10 business days for full forensic package including KV-cache snapshots where applicable.

- Subprocessor pre-approval: Redwood will provide a pre-approved roster of potential subprocessors and the most recent SOC2 reports; if FinBridge pre-approves, those subprocessors can act without additional approval during containment. For any new subprocessor not pre-approved, Redwood will attempt to notify within Stage A and secure retroactive consent where feasible. Vetting receipts will be uploaded into the DocuSign addendum package.

- Delivery mechanics: forensic packages will be delivered via customer-managed S3 or presigned link (7-day expiry) per your preference; chain-of-custody and checksums included. Retention of the snapshot will default to 90 days unless you request a different retention period.

I'll route this to Contracts and share the DocuSign link shortly. Attaching our forensic packaging spec for your review; if you want any additional metadata in the manifest (e.g., token-level telemetry slices), flag it now.

— Marissa
Director, Security & Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachment: forensic_packaging_spec.md
